output.20000: Nominal upper edge of human hearing. Needs a sample rate of about 42.1 kHz or more, so that 20 kHz stays below the digital limit (95 % of Nyquist).

output.title: Frequency
output.body: Frequency is the number of cycles per second, measured in hertz (Hz). Doubling it raises the pitch by one octave.

output.title: Period
output.body: The period is the duration of one cycle: T = 1 / f. Higher frequencies have shorter periods.

output.title: Wavelength
output.body: In air (≈ 343 m/s) the wavelength is λ = 343 / f. 100 Hz spans about 3.4 m; 10 kHz about 3.4 cm.

output.title: Amplitude
output.body: Amplitude is the size of the oscillation. Here it is a relative digital level — not a calibrated sound pressure level.

output.title: Waveform
output.body: The waveform is the shape of one cycle. Sine is pure; triangle, saw and square add harmonics and sound brighter.

output.title: Harmonics
output.body: Harmonics are integer multiples of the fundamental (2f, 3f, …). Square and triangle contain odd harmonics; saw contains all.

output.title: Nyquist limit
output.body: A digital system can represent frequencies only below half its sample rate. Nyquist is a digital limit, not a guarantee of speaker performance.

output.title: Sample rate
output.body: The sample rate is how many values per second the audio system produces. Once audio starts, OSCILLA uses the rate this device reports; until then the display assumes 44.1 kHz provisionally and marks it as such.

output.title: Aliasing
output.body: Content above Nyquist folds back to wrong, lower frequencies. Web Audio oscillators are band-limited, so they omit harmonics above Nyquist instead.

demo.label: Saw at 8 kHz: few harmonics fit

output.title: Modulation
output.body: Modulation means one signal changes a property of another — its level (AM) or its frequency (FM, wobble, siren).

output.title: AM
output.body: Amplitude modulation varies the level. Slow AM is heard as tremolo; fast AM creates sidebands at f ± fm.

output.title: FM
output.body: Frequency modulation varies the frequency. Slow FM is vibrato; audio-rate FM creates many sidebands spaced by the modulation frequency.

output.title: Interference
output.body: When two waves add, they reinforce where they are in phase and cancel where they are out of phase.

output.title: Beating
output.body: Two close frequencies produce a level that rises and falls at their difference: 440 Hz and 442 Hz beat at about 2 Hz.

output.title: Logarithmic perception
output.body: Pitch is perceived roughly by ratios: 100→200 Hz and 1→2 kHz are both one octave and sound like a similar step. That is why sweeps and maps here are logarithmic.

output.title: Human hearing range
output.body: Nominally 20 Hz – 20 kHz. The upper limit commonly falls with age and noise exposure; individual hearing varies widely.

output.title: Ultrasound
output.body: Nominal ultrasound begins above about 20 kHz. 15.5 kHz is a high-frequency signal, not ultrasound. Generating >20 kHz digitally does not mean a speaker emits it.

output.title: Speaker limitations
output.body: Speakers, headphones, DACs and amplifiers can attenuate or distort very low and very high frequencies. Perceived loudness is not a measure of acoustic output.

output.label: Continuous tone
output.desc: Sustained tone while held. Frequency, waveform and gain respond live.

output.label: Finite tone
output.desc: One tone of programmed duration with attack and release ramps.

output.label: Pulse
output.desc: Repeated tone pulses separated by pauses.

output.label: Burst
output.desc: Short tone bursts at a fixed onset-to-onset interval.

output.label: Sweep up
output.desc: Rising sweep from the lower to the higher frequency.

output.label: Sweep down
output.desc: Falling sweep from the higher to the lower frequency.

output.label: Ping-pong sweep
output.desc: Up and down between two frequencies without a gap.

output.label: Chirp
output.desc: A short, fast sweep.

output.label: Siren
output.desc: Frequency moved between two limits by a low-frequency oscillator.

output.label: Alternating
output.desc: Two frequencies in turn.

output.label: Wobble
output.desc: Slow sinusoidal frequency deviation around the center frequency.

output.label: AM tremolo
output.desc: Amplitude modulation: the level rises and falls periodically.

output.label: FM
output.desc: Frequency modulation: a second oscillator moves the carrier frequency.

output.label: Random
output.desc: Random frequencies, uniformly spread on a logarithmic scale. A new sequence follows each play.

output.label: Octave steps
output.desc: Octave steps, by default 125 Hz to 16 kHz; steps above the digital limit are skipped.

output.label: User sequence
output.desc: Your own comma-separated frequencies, e.g. 440, 880, 660, 1.32k.
